frequency_question: How often does an easing cycle or rate reduction occur within a 131-day window under comparable macroeconomic precursor conditions?
membership_rule: Includes all instances from 1950 to present where the Federal Reserve initiated or executed a rate cut within a rolling 131-day observation window during non-crisis and moderate-inflation regimes.
coverage_note: 8 major easing cycle initiations/phases examined; all successfully delivered at least one 25bp cut within a 131-day window once precursor conditions were met.
known_gaps: Excludes emergency unscheduled cuts driven by sudden black swan shocks, focusing on standard policy transition windows.
skeleton: Post-war Fed easing cycles spanning 1950-2024, evaluated by whether rate cuts manifest within rolling 4-month windows during active policy transition phases.
multiplier: 8 historical easing cycles identified in comparable late-cycle or cooling economic configurations over the past 40 years, yielding frequent execution within any given 131-day multi-meeting horizon.
validity_reason: Central bank reaction functions and macroeconomic cycle durations evolve slowly over decades.
